Evaluate a prioritization

Source: R/fct_eval_prioritization.R
eval_prioritization.Rd

Evaluate a prioritization according to how well its represents features, locks, and costs. Additionally, area-based metrics are calculated.

Usage

eval_prioritization(project, settings, prioritization)

Arguments

project

new_project() object to which prioritization should be added.

settings

list of settings used to generate the solution.

prioritization

numeric vector with a value for each planning unit to indicate zone allocations. For example, if the prioritization has three zones, then elements with values ranging between 1 and 3 correspond to planning units that are locked to the three zones (respectively). Additionally, elements with values ranging between 4 and 6 correspond to planning units that are selected as a priority for the three zones (respectively).

Value

A list object. This is a list with a "summary" element that contains a data frame with area-based metrics, as well as "features", "locks", and "costs" elements that contain data frames with metrics for the features, locks, and costs (respectively).

See also

Other functions for prioritization: solve_prioritization()

Examples

# simulate project
sim_project <- simulate_project()

# generate a simulated prioritization
sim_prioritization <- sample.int(
  length(sim_project$zones), sim_project$dataset$get_n_pu(), replace = TRUE
)

# simulate settings to evaluate prioritization
sim_settings <- simulate_prioritization_settings(sim_project)

# evaluate prioritization
eval_prioritization(sim_project, sim_settings, sim_prioritization)
